en: Sārammaṇaduka (The Dyad of Having an Object)
Dependent on a state with nose as its object, a state without nose as its object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state without nose as its object, a state without different objects arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state without nose as its object, states both with nose as their object and without different objects arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with various objects, a state with various objects arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with various objects, a state without an object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with various objects, states both without an object and with various objects arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that has no object and a state that has a different object, there arises a state that has no object by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that has no object and a state that has a different object, there arises a state that has a different object by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that has no object and a state that has a different object, there arise states that have no object and states that have a different object.
They arise with the root condition. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the root;

three in the case of the object; five in the case of the predominance …pe… six in the case of mutuality …pe… one in the case of prenascence and repetition …pe… nine in the case of non-disappearance. (The full detail applies in all cases.)
